 LIVE  Updated  2m ago Will Unwin Tue 3 Nov 2026 16.07 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 3m ago Second half 
 19m ago Half time: Manchester United 0-2 Roma 
 49m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 Roma (Malen, 18) 
 55m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 Roma (Soule, 11) 
 1h ago Kick off 
 2h ago Starting lineups 
 3h ago Preamble 
 Donyell Malen tucks the ball home from the penalty spot to double Roma’s lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Donyell Malen tucks the ball home from the penalty spot to double Roma’s lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Will Unwin Tue 3 Nov 2026 16.07 EST First published on Tue 3 Nov 2026 13.30 EST Share Key events 3m ago Second half 
 19m ago Half time: Manchester United 0-2 Roma 
 49m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 Roma (Malen, 18) 
 55m ago GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 Roma (Soule, 11) 
 1h ago Kick off 
 2h ago Starting lineups 
 3h ago Preamble 
 48s ago 16.07 EST 47 mins: Baleba produces a stunning moment for United and gets through the Roma defence. He looks set to cross for Mbeumo to knock into the net, only to pull up with a hamstring injury. Tielemans is prepared. Baleba looks upset.
 In even worse news for United, Dalot is still on the pitch.
 Pisilli replaces Mora for Roma but United have stuck with the same XI.
 Share 3m ago 16.05 EST Second half
 Can it get any worse for United?
 Share 5m ago 16.03 EST David Johnson quips: “I’m a City fan, and I should be rejoicing, but for the first time in my life I feel sorry for fans of the Forces of Darkness. Keep this up and we’ll be having a Manchester derby in the Northern Premier.”
 Share 9m ago 15.59 EST Surely, Jason Wilcox cannot survive this utter incompetence. 
 Share 9m ago 15.58 EST I am not sure why anyone would want to replace Carrick. Not much going on here.
 Share 12m ago 15.55 EST Jason emails: “The biggest problem is not the ownership. It doesn’t help, but it’s not the main issue. It’s the team building strategy. They spend too much money on too many replacement-level players (offered to them by agents happy to get a payday), and have forgotten that the passion for playing for United comes from a blend of established players and the youth program.
 “Look at the lineup today. Put it in Coventry’s shirts. You wouldn’t be surprised at the results.
 “How many players on this team would have gotten games for Man U during the 1998-99 season? Bruno, the “player of the year,” would have been the 6 th best midfielder, at best. No forward would have played in front of those four great strikers. And the D? No chance.
 “There is Man United’s problem.”
 Share 17m ago 15.50 EST Half-time reading. 
 Phil Foden sets sights on England recall and says he has had no contact with Tuchel Read more Share 19m ago 15.49 EST BOOOOOOOOOO! Comes the sound from the stands. Wilcox and Berrada seek some warmth.
 Share 19m ago 15.48 EST Half time: Manchester United 0-2 Roma
 Another lamentable performance from United who have been outclassed by Roma , aiding the Italians with some utterly pathetic defending. Will Carrick be allowed to limp on until Sunday at this rate?
 Share 21m ago 15.46 EST 45 mins: Malen latches onto a flick on and then thwacks a shot across Lammens who gets down well.
 Two minutes added on.
 Share 22m ago 15.46 EST 44 mins: Fernandes swipes over from 18 yards with his left foot and then complains about the pass not being good enough. He seems frustrated by how bad things are.
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes (left) can’t keep the ball down and it ends up in the crowd. Photograph: Jon Super/AP View image in fullscreen Fernandes is not a happy bunny. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  15.55 EST 23m ago 15.45 EST 43 mins: Eddie Munro writes: “There seem to be many reasons for why United are doing so badly but some I don’t see mentioned enough are that compared to last season, there’s a big Casemiro shaped hole in the midfield (both physically and metaphysically) which means poorer build up play and no protection for the defence and no Sesko to come on as a super-sub to turn draws into wins and defeats into draws (and hide bad performances).
 “Also members of this squad have shown repeatedly in the past that they cannot handle two games a week, either mentally of physically (which is funny considering they were complaining in the 2nd half of last season that they didn’t have enough games to stay fit).
 “Obviously Carrick is trying to change the style of play as well (from mostly counter-attacks to mostly possession) which is what did for Ole. Sack and sell everyone except Carrick and any player under 24 (but sell Zirkzee cos it’s not working) any other solution is just more of the same cycle.”
 Share 24m ago 15.43 EST 42 mins: Malen is booked for pulling back Baleba around 28 yards out. Maybe United should just shoot. Fernandes lines it up … and hits the wall. Everyone go for a half-time pint.
 Share 25m ago 15.42 EST 41 mins: United have enjoyed slightly more possession, so there is that.
 Rob Hopkins emails “Surely Amass isn’t as bad as this, the reluctance to trust a youth player who’s trained and played that position his whole life is worth a shot. Sure, he might make a mistake, but that would be 4 less than Dalot has made in 30 mins.”
 You’d hope not. They were open to selling him in the summer despite the fact they had no other options.
 Share 26m ago 15.41 EST 40 mins: Almost a third for Roma who easily play through United and the ball is set up for Mora to finish but Yoro saves the day.
 Krishnamoorthy writes: “ Now I realise that Jose has gone to Real and am kicking myself for my earlier mail of Jose driving the nail
 “Whoever it is , the problem at United today is not going to be fixed by resting their captain, dropping their goal keeper , or removing their manager - the united problem needs a complete overhaul - and you need a man of SAF’s calibre to build something new from scratch.”
 Share 28m ago 15.40 EST 38 mins: United are working away around the edge of the Roma box but do not look like crating anything. They have yet to test Roma’s third-choice ‘keeper.
 “I really thought with City’s existential crisis that United would revel in former glory but also lay low in terms of drama, instead it’s as if they’ve gone - hold my beer …” says Nicola Schofield . “I can see if City get a points deduction which team they’ll potentially save from relegation!! (May 2027 final plot twist).”
 Share 30m ago 15.38 EST 36 mins: Lulli is booked for a very blatant handball. He seemed genuinely worried if Dalot got beyond him in possession of the ball, he could do some damage. How naive.
 Pramith Pillai emails: “ There is no hope. Carrick doesn’t trust the young defenders, which makes them nervous & uncertain while defending. Our left-back is an aspirational footballer who’s already burned out as a right-back.
 “I hope we’ll get Conte soon. If not, I doubt we’ll win anything in the Championship next year as well.”
 Share 31m ago 15.37 EST 34 mins: Mbeumo gets the wrong side of the Roma defence but is naturally caught and tackled before any danger comes of it. United are just going through the motions now.
 Share 34m ago 15.34 EST 32 mins: To be fair, Cunha is putting in the hard yards here but the chances of it making a difference are slim.
 “I’d be less inclined to blame the 20 year old Ayden Heaven,” writes Andy Donald. “I’d be looking squarely at Dalot for that - he’s been exposing his fellow defenders for many years now. I’d wonder how many goals he has directly been at fault for in the past 10 games. It must be close to 50%. It’s 100% tonight anyway.”
 Share 37m ago 15.31 EST 30 mins: If Malen can show United something, it is that underperforming Dutch strikers can come good. Surely Zirkzee can’t be any worse than this anonymous effort in the final third.
 Stephen Carr emails: “Evening Will, I’m really excited to see Diogo Dalot’s renaissance as a footballer once the Glazer’s sell up ...”
 Kári Tulinius writes: “What a season Roma is having so far! Such a good watch, too. Gianpiero Gasperini has fashioned an exciting, dynamic side out of parts that didn’t fit obviously together. This time they feel like genuine title contenders. Winning Ol’ Big Ears is almost certainly beyond them, but they’ll have a good go.”
 Share 38m ago 15.29 EST 28 mins: Diallo drives into the box and goes down but it is fine tackle from Wesley, even if the United fans think it merits a penalty.
 Share 40m ago 15.27 EST 26 mins: Michael Carrick said people would think he is “crazy” for looking forward to this game. Yes, yes we do.
 Baleba enjoys a respectable one-two with Cunha on the edge of the box but the resulting shot goes well over.
 Share 42m ago 15.25 EST 24 mins: “Sell United and f*** off home” comes the chant around the ground.
 Peter Oh emails: “David Flynn’s shrewd managerial analysis reminds me of something I’ve wondered about for a while. Why, when their team has just conceded, do coaches feel the need to immediately crowd around an iPad? Why don’t they get up to look their players in the eye and encourage them to regroup?
 “It’s as if the screen offers an answer that can’t be discerned from looking at the actual pitch!
 “Game’s gone.”
 Joshua Keeling asks: “How bad will this get? Why is Carrick still there? Why is life so hard?”
 Share 44m ago 15.23 EST 22 mins: The United fans are throwing tennis balls and other items onto the pitch in protest at the ownership and the dreadful way in which the club is being run.
 Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada look miserable.
 Rensch goes off injured and Lulli is on.
 Matthew Lysaght emails: “I would rather have William Prunier than Ayden Heaven at this stage.”
 View image in fullscreen Manchester United's Matheus Cunha collects some of the missiles thrown in protest by fans before disposing of them off the pitch. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA Share Updated at  15.45 EST 46m ago 15.21 EST 20 mins: Soule fumes at Fernandes for United not kicking the ball out for an injury. The Argentinian gets up in the United captain’s face and they both get booked. Poor refereeing.
 Share 47m ago 15.21 EST 18 mins: Dalot gives the ball away in pathetic fashion in his own half and it looks like Roma are in for a third but Heaven puts in a last-ditch tackle.
 Jason Wilcox, why didn’t you sign a backup left-back?
 I was anticipating a day off tomorrow but that is rapidly going out of the window.
 Share 49m ago 15.19 EST GOAL! Manchester United 0-2 Roma (Malen, 18)
 No mistake from the spot as he sends Lammens the wrong way.
 View image in fullscreen Donyell Malen tucks the ball home from the penalty spot to double Roma’s lead. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters View image in fullscreen Malen celebrates his goal in front of disgruntled United fans. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters Share Updated at  15.33 EST 49m ago 15.18 EST 16 mins: PENALTY! Heaven is penalised for blocking a shot with his arm. It all came from Dalot being a mile out of position again.
 Roma have scored 28 goals in 10 Serie A games this season. United may need to worry here based on their utterly woeful defending.
 View image in fullscreen Not much Ayden Heaven could have done about that. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.52 EST 51m ago 15.16 EST 14 mins: United come back at Roma through Fernandes down the right and his cross goes along the six-yard line before Mancini clears, a split second ahead of Cunha meeting the ball.
 Joshua Keeling emails: “How much space?! Where was Dalot?! Outstanding work, United.”
 Share 54m ago 15.14 EST GOAL! United lose the ball in their own half and Roma move at speed, with Mora ping a pass from left to right where Soule is awaiting, helped by Dalot being dreadfully out of position. He gives Lammens the eyes and finds the bottom corner.
 View image in fullscreen Roma's Matias Soule slots the ball past Manchester United's keeper Senne Lammens to open the scoring. Photograph: Jon Super/AP View image in fullscreen Soule celebrates alongside Rodrigo Mora. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  15.22 EST 55m ago 15.13 EST GOAL! Manchester United 0-1 Roma (Soule, 11)
 United are found at the back and Soule does the rest.
 Share 1h ago 15.11 EST 10 mins: Maguire pings a long ball over the top for Fernandes to chase but it lacks the requisite direction and Roma mop up.
 Fernandes, Cunha and Mbeumo seem to be rotating the role of false 9 at the moment, which is a bold move.
 Share 1h ago 15.09 EST 8 mins: Malen looks to do some damage on the edge of the United box but is quickly crowded out and the hosts clear the ball upfield.
 Share 1h ago 15.08 EST 6 mins: Diallo is eager to get on the ball in the early stages. There is positivity around the team and a little more energy that we’ve seen recently. They need the crowd behind them and they are doing their job.
 David Flynn emails: “Nuno wouldn’t fit the bill anyway, it’s experimental European iPad manager next, followed by former player with no managerial experience. So whoever is the Ajax under 18s coach at the moment, then Lee Sharpe.”
 Share 1h ago 15.06 EST 4 mins: United survive the first two minutes without conceded, so that’s a good start.
 Diallo and Cunha combine on the right but the former’s cross is easily blocked.
 Share 1h ago 15.03 EST 2 mins: The United back four is (from left to right) Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Dalot. Good luck, lads.
 Share 1h ago 15.01 EST Kick off
 Peep! Peep! Peep! Here we go!
 Share 1h ago 15.01 EST The players hold a minute’s silence for the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in the second division. 
 Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision Read more Share 1h ago 14.56 EST The players are heading out onto the pitch. 
 Share 1h ago 14.53 EST “We want Glazers out” comes the chant from the Stretford End. 
 Share 1h ago 14.52 EST Plenty of green and gold balloons in the away end as the fans make a point against the owners. The fans want the Glazers out and they are not particularly enamoured with Sir Jim. Two home losses this week will ramp up the toxicity at Old Trafford.
 Share 1h ago 14.45 EST United have conceded in the opening two minutes in their past two Champions League games. Anything better than that would be a boost.
 The players are cheered off after the warmup, which is a start.
 Share 2h ago 14.31 EST Elsewhere … 
 Barcelona v Aston Villa: Champions League – live Read more Share 2h ago 14.26 EST Can United impress Barney Ronay ? 
 Manchester United’s capitulation at Chelsea paints picture of a club that barely exists | Barney Ronay Read more Share 2h ago 14.20 EST Time to get warm. 
 View image in fullscreen Senne Lammens gets ready for the match. Photograph: Paul Currie/Shutterstock Share 2h ago 14.12 EST Michael Carrick: “A big challenge, it’s what you expect. They’ve had a very good start to the season. We want to be in this competition to challenge ourselves against good teams. It’s a big night for us.
 “We have to pick a team, we’ve got good players. We’ve made a decision for tonight.
 “We’ve got some really good midfielders with different strengths. We think it’s a good time to put Kobbie back in with the attributes him and Baleba have.”
 Share 2h ago 14.06 EST Gorton-born Butt on TV and another one on the blog. A big day for east Manchester. Both quite critical of United at the moment.
 Share 2h ago 14.02 EST Gene Salorio asks: “So now that Nuno is back on the market, does he get a ticket to the Manchester United new manager sweepstakes?”
 NO!
 Share 2h ago 14.01 EST Ashley Young suggests if Michael Carrick is forced out, then Jason Wilcox should go too. 
 Something I have suggested, too, and being on this blog is mainly about promoting your own work.
 Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin Read more Share 2h ago 13.58 EST The great John Brewin wrote about how Manchester United have become unmanageable. 
 double quotation mark Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door.
 An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur Read more Share 2h ago 13.57 EST Bit of fun among the team news … Martinez is dropped, allowing us all to guess how the United back four will start off. I feel Yoro deserves a go at centre-back but I will almost certainly be wrong.
 Roma are giving a debut to third-choice goalkeeper Devis Vásquez, who is a 28-year-old who once had a loan at Sheffield Wednesday.
 Share 2h ago 13.55 EST Starting lineups
 Manchester United (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Heaven; Baleba, Mainoo; Diallo, Cunha, Fernandes; Mbeumo
 Subs: Darlow, Heaton, Amass, De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui, Santos, Mount, T Fletcher, Tielemans, Lacey, Zirkzee
 Roma (3-4–2-1): Vazquez; Mancini, Balerdi, Hermoso; Rensch, Cristante, De Roon, Wesley; Soule, Rodrigo Mora; Malen
 Subs: De Marzi, Koulierakis, N’Dicka, Castro, Molina, Pisilli, Di Nunzio, Lulli, Ghilardi
 View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes leads out his teammates to warm up. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.04 EST 2h ago 13.44 EST Ayden Heaven was put up for the pre-match interview – don’t worry he did not say anything on note. The Amazon pundits are perplexed that the young defender forced to face the cameras, with Ashley Young and Wayne Rooney wanting someone more senior to take responsibility.
 Share 2h ago 13.41 EST Roma sit one place above Como in Serie A, which should worry United. 
 Como demolish dismal Manchester United to pile more pressure on Carrick Read more Share 3h ago 13.33 EST I went to see Michael Carrick yesterday for a bit of knockabout fun. 
 Carrick not concerned about Martínez’s attitude as United prepare for Roma visit Read more Share 3h ago 13.30 EST Preamble
 Is this the day Manchester United finally turn their season around and save Michael Carrick’s job? Probably not. The manager is eagerly looking forward to this game despite not winning in nine, sitting 17th in the Premier League and coming into this clash with Roma off the back of two Champions League defeats. Life is not easy for Carrick because he has not fit left-back nor a decent striker available to him, so what can Big Sir Jim really expect?
 Carrick, if we are being honest, has until the final whistle on Sunday - when Aston Villa are in town - to show he can lead United forward. Anything other than two wins this week will almost certainly seal his fate. There were promising signs against Chelsea but that soon unravelled.
 At the very least, Carrick fronts up amid the misery. Those above him say absolutely nothing but must also fear for their futures after a desperate season thus far.
 Kick-off: 8pm GMT
